slides.title: Launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027 as a per-seat Pro plan, not a $149 add-on

paragraphs.text: DISPATCH COPILOT · LAUNCH, PACKAGING AND PRICING
Launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027 as a per-seat Pro plan, not a $149 add-on
Recommendation to CEO Maya Okafor and the executive team for January 2027 planning
Prepared November 2026 · Based only on the Dispatch Copilot briefing pack (the pack states all figures are synthetic benchmark data)
All $ figures are annual recurring revenue (ARR) unless stated; calculations are shown on each slide and in the appendix

slides.title: Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a per-seat Pro plan: it is the only option that lifts NRR toward 105% and keeps gross margin above 75%

paragraphs.text: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a per-seat Pro plan: it is the only option that lifts NRR toward 105% and keeps gross margin above 75%

Recommendation: launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a new Pro plan at +$12 per seat per month ($91 vs $79 Core) with a pooled AI-usage allowance. Do not launch it as a $149 per-account add-on, and make the mobile app rewrite the next engineering priority. Plan on $1.7–2.9M of expansion ARR (+3.0–5.0 NRR points), not the $8M in the proposal.
Launch: a paid Copilot is needed to reach the NRR target, and the beta shows real value
Reaching 105% NRR takes +4 points, about $2.3M of net expansion a year. Removing every mobile-related churn would add only 3.8 points
In the beta, jobs per dispatcher-hour rose 11% against 2% for matched accounts. The gain is real, but volunteer bias inflates it
Routewise now includes AI in its Pro plan. AI explains at most ~$0.6M a year of lost new ARR, a third of Sales’ $1.9M estimate
Packaging and price: a per-seat Pro plan beats the $149 add-on, a free bundle and not launching
Purchases point to 7–14% buying the add-on, not the 46% who said they would: ~$1.2–2.5M ARR, mostly from the heaviest users
Pro at +$12 per seat costs every account 15% more. If 20–33% of accounts move to it: $1.7–2.9M ARR and +3.0–5.0 NRR points
Giving Copilot free in Core cuts company gross margin to 72–74%, below the 75% floor
Trade-offs: accept the two-quarter mobile delay on purpose, protect margin, and launch in stages
The mobile delay loses ~$0.3–0.8M ARR to churn that could have been avoided. Launching Copilot first still reaches 105% about two quarters sooner
An allowance of 500 requests per seat caps AI cost at $4.50 per $12 seat. Company gross margin stays at 76% or more
Test on non-volunteer accounts in Q1 and check results at end of Q3 (go-ahead if ≥13% have moved to Pro). The 14 Copilot engineers move to mobile in Q3 2027
Source: Briefing pack; team analysis. NRR = net revenue retention; GM = gross margin. Ranges reflect the low and high cases set out on slides 7–10.

slides.title: We tested the CPO’s $149 add-on plan against five conditions. Two failed, so we kept the launch but changed the packaging

paragraphs.text: APPROACH · HYPOTHESIS-DRIVEN
We tested the CPO’s $149 add-on plan against five conditions. Two failed, so we kept the launch but changed the packaging
Starting hypothesis (the plan inside the company): launch Copilot in Q2 2027 as a paid add-on at $149 per account per month, worth ~$8M of ARR in year 1.

data: What would have to be true
A. About 46% of accounts buy at $149 (≈$8M ARR)
The survey reached only 6% of admins, and respondents run larger accounts (9.4 seats vs 6.2). In the paywall test, 14% of beta volunteers actually paid
B. A flat price per account pays off at every level of usage
Add-on buyers average 6,800 requests a month ($61 of AI cost). The top 10% average 14,500 ($131), against a $149 price
C. Copilot creates real value for customers
Jobs per dispatcher-hour +11% vs +2% for matched accounts; 4.1 hours a week saved (self-reported); all from volunteers
D. Copilot is needed to hit 105% NRR and to compete
Fixing mobile adds at most 3.8 NRR points. Routewise includes AI in Pro, and our win rate fell from 44% to 37%
SUPPORTED for NRR; competitive effect limited
E. We can afford to delay mobile by two quarters
Mobile is the top churn reason (27%) and the top feature request (38%). A 6-month delay costs ~$0.3–0.8M ARR
PARTLY: only if mobile is next and Customer Success limits the damage

paragraphs.text: Revised answer: Launch in Q2 2027: yes (C, D hold; E holds with conditions). Packaging: change from a $149 per-account add-on to a per-seat Pro plan with a usage allowance (A and B fail).
Source: Briefing pack §4–§8, §10; team analysis.

slides.title: Reaching 105% NRR takes ~$2.3M of net expansion a year. Retention fixes alone cannot get there, so Copilot has to be paid for

paragraphs.text: 1 · WHY LAUNCH
Reaching 105% NRR takes ~$2.3M of net expansion a year. Retention fixes alone cannot get there, so Copilot has to be paid for
NRR points each option could add, low to high case
Needed: +4.0
How we sized the gap
Target: 101% → 105% NRR = +4 pts × $57.6M = $2.30M a year
ARR lost to churn: 14% logo churn × $57.6M ≈ $8.06M a year
Mobile-related: 27% × $8.06M = $2.18M = 3.8 pts maximum
AI-related: 6% × $8.06M = $0.48M = 0.8 pts maximum
Pro: accounts moving × 6.2 seats × $12 × 12 months. 33% → $2.89M (+5.0); 20% → $1.75M (+3.0)
Accounts needed to reach the target alone: Pro 26%; add-on 13%, which is about the beta volunteers’ own buying rate
Pro plan, +$12/seat (20–33% of accounts move)
$149 add-on (7–14% of accounts buy)
Mobile rewrite (prevents 25–75% of mobile churn)
Stop all AI-related churn (0–100%)
Mobile ceiling: even fixing 100% of mobile-related churn adds only 3.8 points. Moving accounts to Pro is a one-off jump, while the mobile fix keeps paying every year. We need both.

Source: Briefing pack §1, §3, §6, §8; team analysis. NRR points = ARR added or retained ÷ $57.6M starting ARR. Assumes accounts that move to Pro or churn are average size (6.2 seats). Mobile-fix share (25–75%) is our assumption; the pack has no estimate.

slides.title: The beta shows a real productivity gain, but the volunteers were larger and more active than typical accounts, so plan on less than the headline

paragraphs.text: 1 · WHY LAUNCH
The beta shows a real productivity gain, but the volunteers were larger and more active than typical accounts, so plan on less than the headline
Change in jobs scheduled per dispatcher-hour vs the prior 12 weeks
Why we discount it
Volunteers: beta accounts average 8.1 seats (vs 6.2) and are more active than the base
Self-reported: the 4.1 hours a week saved is not measured
Concentrated: the top 10% of accounts made 58% of AI requests, so much of the value sits with a few heavy users
+9 pts
net gain vs matched accounts
What it means for the decision
The value is clear even after a heavy discount. At half the hours saved (~8.9 a month), Pro costs an average account ~$8 per dispatcher-hour saved ($4 at the full figure)
Do not assume the full gain in pricing or forecasts. Measure it in non-volunteer accounts in the Q1 test before launch
Beta accounts
Matched non-beta
90-day renewal: 97% for beta accounts vs 93% for matched accounts. This points the right way, but the window is short and the accounts chose to take part.
Source: Briefing pack §5 (Table 1, 240 volunteer accounts, 12 weeks), §11. $/hour = Pro uplift for an average account ($74.40 a month) ÷ dispatcher hours saved a month (4.1 × 52 ÷ 12 = 17.8).

slides.title: Routewise has made AI a must-have, but AI explains at most ~$0.6M a year of lost new ARR, a third of the Sales estimate

paragraphs.text: 1 · WHY LAUNCH
Routewise has made AI a must-have, but AI explains at most ~$0.6M a year of lost new ARR, a third of the Sales estimate
Lost new-customer ARR a year that could be put down to AI ($M)
The calculation
Routewise competes in 60% × 2,600 = 1,560 deals a year
Sales memo: 63% of deals lost × 1,560 = 983 lost; a third of them = 328 deals × $5,878 = $1.93M
Why the Sales memo overstates it
Mentioning AI in a loss note (31%) does not show AI caused the loss, and we were already losing 56% of these deals before Routewise had AI
Routewise also offered 20% off the first year in Q3 2026, the same quarter the win rate fell
Implication: Copilot in Pro is needed to defend against Routewise’s Pro plan, but the case must not count more than ~$0.6M of new ARR from it

Sales memo:
"a third of lost deals"
Upper limit: AI caused the whole 7-pt drop in win rate
If half the drop came from Routewise’s price cut
Source: Briefing pack §7, §10, §11; team analysis. New account = 6.2 seats × $79 × 12 = $5,878 ARR. New-customer ARR does not count toward NRR.

slides.title: Of four ways to package Copilot, only the per-seat Pro plan meets both the NRR objective and the gross-margin floor

paragraphs.text: 2 · PACKAGE & PRICE
Of four ways to package Copilot, only the per-seat Pro plan meets both the NRR objective and the gross-margin floor

data: Price increase for an average account
2023 tier launch: 33% moved in a year

paragraphs.text: On ARR alone Pro and the add-on overlap: Pro earns more only if over ~21% of accounts move (the add-on central case is 10.7% → $1.87M). Pro wins on the other criteria: it matches Routewise, charges every account the same share and keeps AI cost under control.

Source: Briefing pack; team analysis. Year-1 run rate. Gross margin is company-wide, with the $0.6M platform cost in cost of revenue. Pro AI cost is at the full allowance (3,100 requests per average account). Payback = $1.47M engineering cost ÷ annual gross profit from the option.

slides.title: A pooled allowance of 500 AI requests per Pro seat keeps company gross margin at 76% or more, even if heavy users all move to Pro

paragraphs.text: 2 · PACKAGE & PRICE
A pooled allowance of 500 AI requests per Pro seat keeps company gross margin at 76% or more, even if heavy users all move to Pro
Company gross margin by option (%)
75% floor
How the allowance protects margin
Cap: 500 requests × $0.009 = $4.50 of AI cost per $12 seat, so at least 62% of the uplift is kept before platform cost
Pooled across the account: an average 6.2-seat account gets 3,100 requests, more than the median beta account uses (1,900)
Heavy users pay: packs of 10,000 requests at $200 a month ($0.02 per request, 55% margin)
Without it: if Pro accounts use as much as add-on buyers, margin falls to 74.1%, below the floor
Possible gain from 2028: our price is fixed to December 2027. If the provider’s 35% fall in list prices carries through, cost per request falls to $0.0059 and margin rises to ~76.9%
Today (Core only)
Pro with allowance, 20% move
Pro with allowance, 33% move
$149 add-on, 14% buy
Pro, no allowance, heavy use
Free in Core, 50% use it
Free in Core, all use it
The scale starts at 70% so the gaps are visible; each dot is a single company-wide figure.

Source: Briefing pack §1, §3, §5, §6; team analysis. Company GM = (today’s $44.9M gross profit + new revenue − AI cost − $0.6M platform) ÷ (today’s $57.6M + new revenue). "Heavy use" assumes Pro accounts use as much as add-on buyers (6,800 requests a month).

slides.title: Launching Copilot first costs ~$0.3–0.8M of ARR to mobile churn. On ARR it is a close call, but it is the only order that reaches 105% NRR by H1 2028

paragraphs.text: 3 · TRADE-OFFS & PLAN
Launching Copilot first costs ~$0.3–0.8M of ARR to mobile churn. On ARR it is a close call, but it is the only order that reaches 105% NRR by H1 2028

data: ~$0.27–0.82M to mobile churn (25–75% of $2.18M a year × 0.5 years)
Up to ~$0.56M: ≤$0.32M of new ARR to Routewise + ≤$0.24M of AI-related churn (upper limits)
Builds from Q2 2027 to $1.7–2.9M ARR by Q2 2028
$0.9–1.4M of Pro revenue arrives later (Pro ARR × 0.5 years)
Lands two quarters later; the 14 engineers join it in Q3 2027
Late 2028 at best, likely to slip

paragraphs.text: How to limit the mobile cost
Customer Success outreach: contact accounts that have raised mobile complaints, the 27% churn group
Publish a dated mobile roadmap so customers can see the fix is coming
Copilot’s 14 engineers move to mobile in Q3 2027 after launch; no follow-on AI features ahead of mobile
Keep the launch to the three beta features, so the 14-engineer, two-quarter estimate holds
Track mobile-related churn monthly; if it rises above the 2026 rate, raise it at the Q3 review

Our view: on permanent ARR this is a close call, and doing mobile first may lose slightly less. What decides it is timing: only Copilot first gives Pro time to deliver its uplift before the 2028 NRR target, while Routewise’s AI is still new. The mobile fix then keeps NRR up once the one-off Pro gain is used up.

Source: Briefing pack §3, §7–§9, §11; team analysis. Assumes doing mobile first delays Copilot by the same two quarters (same engineering capacity) and that the rewrite prevents 25–75% of mobile-related churn ($2.18M a year). Deferred revenue = Pro ARR × 0.5 years.

slides.title: We ask the executive team for five decisions in January planning

We ask the executive team for five decisions in January planning
